task_name: The spec's committed copy on the default branch

rubric.result: The objective promises that 'the backend can say whether the execution spec is readable on the repository's default branch'. Taken apart: (a) a way to ask the question — `PublishedSpecs.holds({ repository, path }): Promise<boolean>` in `backend/src/domain/ports/published-specs.ts`; (b) something that answers it against GitHub — `GhPublishedSpecs.holds` runs `['api', 'repos/<owner>/<name>/contents/<encoded path>']` with no `ref`, so GitHub answers for the default branch, and returns `true` on exit 0; (c) the distinction D-23 needs between 'not merged yet' and 'the tool is broken' — `Gh.isNotFound(outcome.stderr)` (regex `/\(HTTP 404\)/`) turns the 404 into `false` and every other failure into `PublishedSpecNotRead` carrying gh's own stderr; (d) that leaf reaching the wire — `PlanCollapse` maps it to `published-spec-not-read` in `start-plan-route.ts`. Each part is produced by a line of the diff. Nothing the objective names is missing, and the diff produces nothing the objective did not name.

The **TDD:** line names `it('a spec github cannot find on the default branch is not published and is no failure')`, with the scripted gh exiting 1 with `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`, `holds` answering `false` and nothing thrown. The diff's test arranges exactly that input — `GhDouble.answering(1, { stderr: RealGhAnswers.SPEC_ABSENT_FROM_THE_DEFAULT_BRANCH })` with that constant set to `'gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)'` — and asserts `await expect(gh.holds()).resolves.toBe(false)`, which pins both halves of the sentence: the same expected value (`false`) and 'nothing thrown' (a rejection fails `resolves`). Its declared boundary pair is present with the plan's name, the plan's input (exit 1, `gh: To use GitHub CLI, run: gh auth login`) and the plan's expected value (`toBeInstanceOf(PublishedSpecNotRead)` plus `expect(refusal.message).toContain('gh: To use GitHub CLI, run: gh auth login')` — 'carrying that line'). Same assertion, same input, same expected value.

Three Contract blocks, compared symbol by symbol. `published-specs.ts`: `export class PublishedSpecs` with `async holds({ repository, path }: { repository: RepositoryName, path: string }): Promise<boolean>` — parameter names, destructuring, types and return shape are literally what the block states; the body follows `epic-specs.ts`'s 'must implement' idiom. `gh-published-specs.ts`: `export class GhPublishedSpecs extends PublishedSpecs`, `constructor({ gh }: { gh: Gh })` calling `super()`, and `static argvFor({ repository, path }: { repository: RepositoryName, path: string }): string[]` — the same names, the same order, the same visibility (public static, as the block writes it and as `GhPlanIssues.argvFor` and `GhUserStories.argvFor` already do). `gh.ts`: `static readonly #NOT_FOUND = /\(HTTP 404\)/` and `static isNotFound(stderr: string): boolean` are character-for-character the block's two lines, placed beside `Gh.labelMissingIn` as the prose asks. The prose's other named values also hold: exit 0 is `true`, the 404 is `false`, anything else raises `PublishedSpecNotRead` with gh's own message, each path segment is percent-encoded (`path.split('/').map(encodeURIComponent).join('/')`), and the leaf joins `PlanCollapse` under the literal constant `'published-spec-not-read'`.

Row by row. D-10 (everything new under `backend/` is TypeScript): both new modules are `.ts`, implemented with the value the row states. D-11 (a yardstick is imported from the plugin, never reimplemented): the diff grows no second opinion about the freeze or the groom; it asks gh a question. D-23 (the groom waits for the spec's committed copy on the **default** branch): implemented with that value — no `ref` is sent, which is the whole point of the third verification command, and `spec-link.js`'s `?ref=` precedent is deliberately not copied. D-13 (no phase is stored): the answer is derived from a live read, nothing is written. D-6, D-7, D-18, D-21, D-22, D-25, D-1, D-14 and the closing row bear on the presses, the front and the coordinating session; this diff touches none of them and so leaves those rows alone. No row is reopened.

Exemplars: `backend/src/domain/ports/epic-specs.ts` — the new port matches its idiom (a class whose methods throw a message naming the method and quoting what it was asked about). `backend/src/infrastructure/gh-pull-requests.ts` and `gh-plan-issues.ts` — the new adapter matches theirs: `extends` its port, `readonly gh: Gh` injected by name through the constructor, a static argv builder, `this.gh.run(argv, { safeToRepeat: true })` for a read, `outcome.failed` interpreted rather than caught, and a throw whose message is `${Gh.BIN} ... failed: ${outcome.stderr.trim()}` — the same sentence `GhPullRequests.#read` writes. `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/gh-plan-issues.test.ts` — the new test file mirrors its `GhDouble`: a real `Gh` whose `launch` records argv and answers a `ProcessOutput`, a real `RetryPolicy`/`RetryBudget`, a `SleepDouble`, and assertions on the literal argv. Rules read and applied: `conventions/defects.md` (four verdicts below), `style.md` (no comment or docstring anywhere in the diff; every identifier, test name and diagnostic in English, as `CLAUDE.md` also demands; no free function — everything hangs off `PublishedSpecs`, `GhPublishedSpecs`, `Gh`, `RealGhAnswers` or `GhDouble`), `architecture.md` (the port under `domain/ports/`, the adapter under `infrastructure/`; the domain imports nothing from the other layers — `published-specs.ts` imports only `type RepositoryName`; one concept per module; the folder, not a suffix, is the discriminator), `domain.md` (the port speaks no tool's language: `PublishedSpecs.holds` survives swapping gh for the REST API unchanged; a separate port is licensed by 'a collaborator is identified by what is asked of it' — 'is this path readable on the default branch' is not the question `PullRequests` or `PlanIssues` ask; and `backend/conventions/this-repository.md`'s 'every family names its two causes' holds because the leaf joins `SpecFreezeFailure`, which already carries both `*NotRead` and `*NotUnderstood`), `boundaries.md` (the failure of the external system is data — the exit code and stderr are read, not caught; no cast, no boundary model needed because stdout is never parsed; the cap arrives injected inside `Gh`, not chosen by the adapter; the adapter is named after its implementation, `Gh` + `PublishedSpecs`; the code of the answer is declared explicitly beside `PublishedSpecNotRead` in `PlanCollapse` rather than derived from the class name), `decisions.md` (the 404 marker exists once, in `Gh.#NOT_FOUND`; the plugin's `spec-link.js` builds a human blob url with an explicit `?ref=`, a different question with no business change forcing both at once — idiom, not a spread rule), `simplicity.md` (nothing added that today's problem does not need: no `ref` parameter, no stdout parse, no defensive branch; `argvFor` is public because the Contract block states it and because the repo's own argv builders are public). Boundaries: the yardstick's sentences on the outer edge are the ones quoted above and the diff answers them. Delivery: the change is purely additive — a new port, a new adapter, a new exception leaf and one new row in `PlanCollapse`'s map; no existing signature, constructor or public contract is altered and no call site is left on an old path, so no document's sentence about expand-contract or gating has a subject here. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — no subject that this rule condemns; the only new value is `holds`'s boolean, and it is a genuine two-state predicate ('the default branch holds this path, or it does not'), not a vocabulary collapsed into a boolean: the third state, 'gh could not answer', is kept separate as `PublishedSpecNotRead` rather than folded into `false`, which is exactly the distinction the rule exists to preserve, and no string is compared by hand and no dispatch has a catch-all. (2) raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: the port returns a boolean and the adapter returns a boolean; nothing hands a map to a module that decides with it. (3) two fields that have to agree — no subject: one field, no flag repeating another, and no sentinel standing for an absence (the 'not published' case is a value of the answer and the 'tool broke' case is a typed error, neither of them an empty string or a zero). (4) an error named for where it happens — `PublishedSpecNotRead` is named for what happens, not for the module (`GhPublishedSpecs`) or the tool (`gh`), and it inherits from the family that fits it rather than from the root `PlanFailure`. One yardstick note, declared rather than filed as a finding: `conventions/testing.md` requires an adapter's declared output shape to come from a real capture, and the implementer reports that the boundary-pair fixture `gh: To use GitHub CLI, run: gh auth login` is the string the plan prescribes verbatim while a live logged-out gh on that machine prints something else. The plan's **TDD:** line pins that literal, so plan and document cannot both be satisfied; the implementer honoured the plan, kept that test outside the `describe(RealGhAnswers.CAPTURE)` block whose provenance declaration covers the two genuinely captured cases, and declared the gap. It also costs nothing here, since the adapter branches on `(HTTP 404)` and not on that line's text.

Does not apply: the staged diff is 139 insertions and 0 deletions across six files (`6 files changed, 139 insertions(+)`), and the only test file in it, `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/gh-published-specs.test.ts`, is new. There is no `-` line anywhere, so no pre-existing assertion, case or test was removed, relaxed or rewritten. I also checked the one pre-existing test the new exception could have weakened without a `-` line — `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/plan-refusal.test.ts`, whose `every_way_the_plan_can_collapse_has_a_refusal_declared...` compares `PlanCollapse.declaredFailures()` against every `PlanFailure` descendant — and it stays as strict as it was: the new leaf is declared in `PlanCollapse`, so the equality still holds without that file being touched.

The promised behaviour lives in production code, not in the test's scaffolding. The percent-encoding is `path.split('/').map(encodeURIComponent).join('/')` in `gh-published-specs.ts`; the url with no `ref` is built there too; `true`/`false` come from `outcome.failed` and `Gh.isNotFound(outcome.stderr)`, with `#NOT_FOUND` living in `gh.ts`; the raise is `throw new PublishedSpecNotRead(...)` in the adapter. The test file supplies only the exit code and the stderr line the scripted gh prints, and asserts on what the production code did with them — the argv it built (`expect(gh.calls).toEqual([...])`), the value it returned and the error it threw. Revert any of those production lines and each of the four tests falls.

The six touched paths are exactly the six the **Files:** line declares, and what is written inside them traces back sentence by sentence: `published-specs.ts` and `gh-published-specs.ts` are the two Contract blocks; `gh.ts` gains only `#NOT_FOUND` and `isNotFound`, which the third Contract block states; `exceptions.ts` gains one line, `PublishedSpecNotRead`, which the task's prose names; `start-plan-route.ts` gains only the import and the map row for 'The leaf joins `PlanCollapse` as `published-spec-not-read`'; the test file holds the four tests **Tests:** lists and nothing else. Nothing named in `### Out of scope` is touched: `ct-groom.mjs`, `groom.js`, `slices.js` and `gh-issue-map.js` are untouched, no `--reconcile`/`--project`, no dispatcher or gate-1 behaviour changed, no write to a pull request, no repository column. No refactor, rename or adjacent fix rides along — the diff has zero deletions. The plan file `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-14-issue-330-the-groom-and-gate-2.md` is **not** in the diff, so there is no amendment to rule on; I read its Task 2 section in the repository and it is word for word the brief's, verification commands and test names included. `backend/API.md` is not updated, and correctly so: the plan assigns it to task 10 and it is not in this task's **Files:**.

Four new tests, all in the new file, measured on the three properties. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no network, no randomness and no sleep — the only path used is a string in an argv that is never opened, `Gh`'s waits go through `SleepDouble.sleep`, and the scripted failures are non-transient (`RetryPolicy.afterAFailure` returns `retry: false` when `transient` is false), so the call count is fixed. Isolated: every test builds its own `GhDouble`, which builds its own `Gh`, `RetryPolicy` and `SleepDouble`; nothing is shared, mutated across tests or ordered — the two class-level constants are frozen strings. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are on what the adapter returned (`resolves.toBe(false)`, `resolves.toBe(true)`), on what it threw (`toBeInstanceOf(PublishedSpecNotRead)`, `message` containing gh's line) and on the literal request it sent (`expect(gh.calls).toEqual([['api', 'repos/mercadona/control-tower/contents/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-11%20the%20loop.md']])`) — never on a mock's call count or a constant the test just defined, and none of them survives reverting this diff's production lines. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` and re-read its 'Testing Anti-Patterns' section and `conventions/testing.md` for the finer half, and found no sentence of either that these tests contradict: each name is a sentence about what is guaranteed rather than the method called, each test covers one behaviour, the double is scoped to what it doubles, and the provenance of the captured shape is declared in `RealGhAnswers.CAPTURE` over the describe that uses it. Nothing reportable, at any severity.
